Protein per 100 grams.Apple: About 85% of an apple is water, and roughly a quarter of its volume is air, which is why apples float in a barrel.
Protein per 100 grams.Banana: Bananas are botanically berries, and they are very slightly radioactive thanks to their potassium-40.
Protein per 100 grams.Cooked white rice: Rice feeds roughly half the world, but its low protein is why rice-based diets are usually paired with beans, fish or eggs.
Protein per 100 grams.Whole milk: Around 80% of milk protein is casein, the same stuff that clumps into curds when milk is turned into cheese.
Protein per 100 grams.Cooked lentils: Lentils were farmed in the Near East over 8,000 years ago, making them one of the oldest crops, and they are a protein staple across South Asia.
Protein per 100 grams.Egg: Egg white was long the benchmark for protein quality in nutrition science because the body uses it so efficiently.
Protein per 100 grams.Peanuts: Peanuts are legumes, not nuts. They ripen underground, which explains why their protein content rivals that of beans.
Protein per 100 grams.Cooked chicken breast: Raw chicken breast has only about 22 g of protein per 100 g. Cooking drives off water and concentrates it to around 31 g.
Protein per 100 grams.Parmesan: Aged for a year or two, Parmesan loses water and its proteins break down into amino acids, and the crunchy specks inside are tyrosine crystals.
Protein per 100 grams.Dried spirulina: Spirulina is a blue-green bacterium, not a true alga, and space agencies have studied it as astronaut food. Dried, it is over half protein, but servings are small.

Keyboard history.Remington No. 1 typewriter: Sholes and Glidden's machine only typed capitals, but its QWERTY layout, set here, has survived 150 years.
Keyboard history.Dvorak layout patented: August Dvorak and William Dealey patented a layout that promised faster typing, though studies have found little real advantage.
Keyboard history.IBM Selectric: This typewriter used a spinning typeball instead of metal arms, so you could switch fonts just by swapping the ball.
Keyboard history.IBM Model F (IBM PC): The first IBM PC shipped with a keyboard that used buckling springs, giving a loud, crisp click.
Keyboard history.IBM Model M: Built with buckling springs, this IBM keyboard was so tough that Unicomp still sells updated versions today.
Keyboard history.First Windows key: The Natural Keyboard from Microsoft added a split design and the Windows key, the first key dedicated to the operating system.
Keyboard history.Happy Hacking Keyboard: Created by computer scientist Eiiti Wada, this compact keyboard stripped out extra keys and became a favorite among programmers.
Keyboard history.Colemak layout: Shai Coleman's layout keeps Z, X, C and V where they sit on QWERTY so that common shortcuts are unchanged.
Keyboard history.Apple butterfly keyboard: Introduced with the slim 12-inch MacBook, it was prone to sticking and failing, and was replaced in 2019 and 2020.
Keyboard history.Copilot key: Announced by Microsoft in January 2024, this was the first major change to the Windows PC keyboard layout in about 30 years.

When these speed barriers fell.Car tops 100 km/h: Camille Jenatzy's electric car, called La Jamais Contente, was the first to pass 100 km/h in 1899, shaped like a torpedo.
When these speed barriers fell.Train tops 200 km/h: A German electric railcar test run reached about 210 km/h in 1903, a speed regular service would only match decades later.
When these speed barriers fell.Car tops 100 mph: Barney Oldfield and others set records in these early years, when 100 mph still seemed utterly terrifying on open roads.
When these speed barriers fell.Car tops 300 mph: Malcolm Campbell took his Blue Bird across Daytona Beach sands in 1935, pioneering high-speed record attempts on flat natural surfaces.
When these speed barriers fell.Plane breaks the sound barrier: Chuck Yeager flew the rocket-powered Bell X-1 past Mach 1 in October 1947, and the achievement was kept secret for months.
When these speed barriers fell.Plane reaches Mach 2: Scott Crossfield reached this speed in the Douglas Skyrocket in 1953, becoming the first pilot to fly at twice the speed of sound.
When these speed barriers fell.Plane reaches Mach 3: The Bell X-2 hit Mach 3 in 1956, but its pilot Milburn Apt was killed after losing control, a reminder of the era's danger.
When these speed barriers fell.Train tops 500 km/h: A French TGV test train hit 515 km/h in 1990, showing that steel wheels on rails could keep going faster than anyone expected.
When these speed barriers fell.Car breaks the sound barrier: The jet-powered ThrustSSC became the first land vehicle to break the sound barrier in 1997, with a top speed of about 1,228 km/h.
When these speed barriers fell.Train tops 600 km/h: Japan's maglev train reached 603 km/h in 2015, floating on magnets above its track rather than running on wheels.

Legendary boxing fights.Dempsey-Tunney Long Count: Dempsey, after being floored, was slow to retreat to a neutral corner, so the count was delayed by several seconds, helping Tunney get up.
Legendary boxing fights.Louis-Schmeling rematch: Joe Louis knocked Max Schmeling out in the first round at Yankee Stadium, a victory in front of a world watching with tension on the eve of war.
Legendary boxing fights.Ali-Frazier Fight of Century: Called the Fight of the Century, it was the first meeting of two undefeated heavyweight champions, and Frazier won on points at Madison Square Garden.
Legendary boxing fights.Rumble in the Jungle: Muhammad Ali beat George Foreman in Zaire with his rope-a-dope tactic, letting the champion punch himself out before knocking him down.
Legendary boxing fights.Thrilla in Manila: The third Ali-Frazier fight was so brutal in the heat that Frazier's trainer stopped it before the last round, and Ali said it was the closest to death he'd felt.
Legendary boxing fights.Hagler vs Hearns: This three-round war, often called the greatest first round in boxing history, is remembered for the relentless exchange from both fighters.
Legendary boxing fights.Tyson vs Spinks: Mike Tyson destroyed Michael Spinks in 91 seconds in Atlantic City, and it was the high point of his unbeaten championship run.
Legendary boxing fights.Holyfield-Tyson bite fight: Tyson bit off part of Evander Holyfield's ear in the third round, and was disqualified in one of the sport's most notorious moments.
Legendary boxing fights.Mayweather vs Pacquiao: Dubbed the Fight of the Century, it became the richest boxing match to that point, with Mayweather winning a unanimous decision.
Legendary boxing fights.Mayweather vs McGregor: Mayweather, a boxing champion, took on a UFC star in a crossover bout that Mayweather won by stoppage in the tenth round.

Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Blu-ray laser: Its blue-violet beam has a shorter wavelength than a DVD's red one, so it can read finer pits and fit far more data per disc.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Argon-ion laser: Its blue-green beam has been used in eye surgery and light shows, and for years it was a workhorse of laboratory science.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Green laser pointer: Most are really infrared lasers whose light is doubled in frequency by a crystal, so cheap ones can leak invisible infrared.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Sodium street lamp: Its near-single-colour yellow glow made streets look orange and was easy for astronomers to filter out; LEDs are replacing these lamps.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Helium-neon laser: Built in 1960 by Ali Javan, it was the first continuous gas laser, and it long powered supermarket barcode scanners.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Hydrogen-alpha line: The red glow of excited hydrogen explains why many nebulae look red in photographs, and special filters let telescopes image the Sun's surface.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Ruby laser: Theodore Maiman built the first working laser from a ruby crystal in 1960.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Nd:YAG laser: Invisible infrared light with a neodymium-doped crystal, it is used in surgery, tattoo removal and welding.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.Fibre-optic telecom: Glass fibre is most transparent near this wavelength, so signals can cross oceans with relatively few boosts.
Lasers and light sources by wavelength.CO₂ laser: It emits far infrared and is a workhorse for industrial cutting, able to cut steel, wood and acrylic.

When these famous figures died.Hammurabi: Babylon's king had his law code carved on a basalt stele now in the Louvre, famed for 'an eye for an eye'.
When these famous figures died.Ramesses II: He ruled for 66 years and fought at Kadesh; his mummy was issued a passport to travel to Paris in 1976.
When these famous figures died.Socrates: Condemned to drink hemlock for impiety and corrupting youth, he is known to us mainly through Plato.
When these famous figures died.Alexander the Great: He died in Babylon at 32, and with no clear heir, his empire split among his generals, who went on to fight one another.
When these famous figures died.Archimedes: He was killed by a Roman soldier during the siege of Syracuse, and he's remembered for shouting 'Eureka' in his bath.
When these famous figures died.Julius Caesar: Senators stabbed him on the Ides of March, and he reportedly had 23 wounds, with the Roman Republic then spiralling into civil war.
When these famous figures died.Nero: His suicide ended the Julius-Claudian dynasty, and the Year of Four Emperors followed.
When these famous figures died.Constantine the Great: He was baptized on his deathbed, and he moved the capital to Byzantium, renamed Constantinople.
When these famous figures died.Marco Polo: After he dictated his travels from a Genoese prison, he reportedly said on his deathbed that he had not told half of what he saw.
When these famous figures died.Joan of Arc: She was burned at Rouen at about 19 and was declared innocent in a retrial; the Church made her a saint in 1920.

Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.The Ritz Paris: César Ritz's hotel was among the first with private bathrooms, and Coco Chanel lived there for years.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Hilton: Conrad Hilton bought his first hotel in Cisco, Texas, hoping to profit from the oil boom, and later built a global chain.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Marriott: It began as a root beer stand in Washington, D.C., run by J. Willard Marriott and his wife, before they added hotels.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Best Western: It is a cooperative of independently owned hotels rather than a single company.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Holiday Inn: Kemmons Wilson founded it in Memphis after a disappointing family road trip.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Hyatt: Jay Pritzker bought a motel by Los Angeles airport and began the chain, which is named for that hotel.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Four Seasons: Founded by Isadore Sharp in Toronto, the chain built its name on service and has long focused on luxury.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Motel 6: The original rooms cost six dollars a night, which gave the motel chain its name, though prices have since risen a lot.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Ibis: Accor's budget brand takes its name from the sacred ibis, a bird that was revered in ancient Egypt.
Where to stay: hotel brands by founding.Airbnb: The founders rented air mattresses in their San Francisco apartment, hence the name AirBed & Breakfast.

When these dolls first came out.Kewpie: Illustrator Rose O'Neill's cherubs first appeared in a magazine in 1909, and the name Kewpie is a playful twist on Cupid.
When these dolls first came out.Raggedy Ann: Johnny Gruelle's rag doll came with a story that his daughter Marcella found the original in an attic.
When these dolls first came out.Barbie: Named after Ruth Handler's daughter Barbara, she debuted at the 1959 New York Toy Fair; her boyfriend Ken is named for Handler's son.
When these dolls first came out.Baby Alive: Made by Kenner, this doll shocked parents by really eating, drinking and needing a nappy change.
When these dolls first came out.Strawberry Shortcake doll: The scented doll grew out of American Greetings card art for a fruity-smelling character in a red-and-white outfit.
When these dolls first came out.My Little Pony: Hasbro's pony toys later found a huge adult fan base, known as bronies, after the 2010 series Friendship Is Magic.
When these dolls first came out.Sylvanian Families: Little woodland animal families made by Epoch in Japan; they are sold as Calico Critters in North America.
When these dolls first came out.American Girl: Pleasant Rowland created them to teach history, with each doll sold alongside books about a girl growing up in a past era.
When these dolls first came out.Polly Pocket: Chris Wiggs made it for his young daughter as a tiny doll in a clamshell compact, and the idea shrank toys to pocket size.
When these dolls first came out.Monster High: Mattel's line of monster teenagers, such as Draculaura and Frankie Stein, was created by designer Garrett Sander.

When these hit singles came out.Johnny B. Goode: Chuck Berry's opening guitar riff is among rock's most imitated, and the song was sent into space on Voyager's Golden Record.
When these hit singles came out.I Want to Hold Your Hand: The Beatles' first US No. 1 set off Beatlemania in America after their Ed Sullivan appearance in early 1964.
When these hit singles came out.Bohemian Rhapsody: Queen's six-minute single has no chorus, and it returned to the charts after 1992's Wayne's World.
When these hit singles came out.Billie Jean: Michael Jackson first moonwalked on television while performing it at the Motown 25 special.
When these hit singles came out.Smells Like Teen Spirit: Nirvana's breakout was named after a deodorant brand a friend mentioned; it brought grunge into the mainstream.
When these hit singles came out....Baby One More Time: Britney Spears's debut single, written by Max Martin, hit No. 1 around the world when she was 16.
When these hit singles came out.Crazy in Love: Beyonce's first solo No. 1, built on a horn riff sampled from the Chi-Lites and a guest verse from Jay-Z.
When these hit singles came out.Rolling in the Deep: Adele co-wrote it after a breakup, and it won the Grammys for both Record and Song of the Year.
When these hit singles came out.Uptown Funk: Mark Ronson and Bruno Mars's funk hit spent 14 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
When these hit singles came out.Blinding Lights: The Weeknd's synth-pop hit was named Billboard's greatest Hot 100 hit of all time in 2021.

E-numbers of these food additives.Curcumin (turmeric color): Turmeric's yellow pigment, found in curry and mustard, takes the very first slot in the E-number system.
E-numbers of these food additives.Caramel color: The most widely used food coloring in the world, it gives colas their brown.
E-numbers of these food additives.Vitamin C: Its chemical name is ascorbic acid, and 'ascorbic' means 'anti-scurvy'.
E-numbers of these food additives.Lecithin: Often derived from soy, sunflower or egg yolk, it helps oil and water mix in chocolate and mayonnaise.
E-numbers of these food additives.Citric acid: It gives lemons their sourness, but industry makes it by fermenting sugar with the mold Aspergillus niger.
E-numbers of these food additives.Guar gum: Made from the seeds of a legume grown mostly in India, it thickens ice cream and sauces.
E-numbers of these food additives.Pectin: Naturally present in apples and citrus peel, it's what makes jam set.
E-numbers of these food additives.Baking soda: Sodium bicarbonate releases carbon dioxide when heated or mixed with acid, which makes cakes rise.
E-numbers of these food additives.MSG: A salt of glutamic acid, found naturally in tomatoes and Parmesan, first isolated by Kikunae Ikeda in 1908, who named the taste umami.
E-numbers of these food additives.Aspartame: About 200 times sweeter than sugar, it was discovered by accident in 1965 by a chemist testing an ulcer drug.

Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.D ring: This faint, inner ring begins close to Saturn's cloud tops and was discovered only through spacecraft images.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.C ring: This dim ring was once called the crepe ring, and its relatively transparent look lets you see Saturn through it.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.B ring: The brightest and densest main ring, so thick that stars can be hidden behind it.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.Cassini Division: This 4,800 km wide gap is named for the astronomer who found it in 1675, and it isn't truly empty.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.A ring: Visible even from a small telescope, this is the outermost of the main rings, and it contains the Encke Gap.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.Encke Gap: This narrow gap in the A ring is kept clear by the tiny moon Pan, which orbits within it.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.F ring: Two small moons, Prometheus and Pandora, shepherd this thin ring and pull on its strands.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.G ring: A faint, dusty ring discovered by Voyager, which is mostly invisible except when seen with the Sun behind it.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.E ring: This broad, diffuse ring is fed by icy geysers from the moon Enceladus.
Saturn's rings and gaps, from Saturn out.Phoebe ring: Discovered in 2009, this enormous and nearly invisible ring is so wide it could hold about a billion Earths.

How we listened: music formats by launch.Edison's phonograph: Edison's invention recorded sound on a tinfoil cylinder, and his first words were reportedly "Mary had a little lamb."
How we listened: music formats by launch.Berliner's gramophone disc: Emile Berliner's flat disc design became the basis for the records that dominated music for the next century.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Vinyl LP: The long-playing record from Columbia packed about 22 minutes per side, and it let albums become an art form.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Compact cassette: Philips introduced the compact cassette in 1963, and it made recording music at home easy and mixtapes possible.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Sony Walkman: Sony's portable cassette player let people carry music on a walk, and it changed how we listened.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Compact disc: This disc was developed by Philips and Sony and stores sound digitally, and the first CD ever pressed was ABBA's The Visitors.
How we listened: music formats by launch.MiniDisc: Sony's recordable mini optical disc was popular in Japan, but flash drives and MP3 players made it obsolete.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Napster: Shawn Fanning built it as a teenager, and it let people share MP3 files, which upended the industry.
How we listened: music formats by launch.iPod: Apple launched this with the slogan 1,000 songs in your pocket, and it became the best-selling music player ever.
How we listened: music formats by launch.Spotify: This Swedish streaming service made music rented rather than owned, and it has over 600 million users.

The first ten US presidents.George Washington: Elected unanimously by the Electoral College twice, a feat no other president has repeated.
The first ten US presidents.John Adams: The first president to live in the White House; he died on 4 July 1826, the same day as Jefferson.
The first ten US presidents.Thomas Jefferson: Wrote the Declaration of Independence; his tombstone lists that and founding the University of Virginia, not the presidency.
The first ten US presidents.James Madison: Known as the 'Father of the Constitution'; he was about 5 feet 4 inches tall.
The first ten US presidents.James Monroe: His Monroe Doctrine of 1823 warned Europe off the Americas, and Liberia's capital, Monrovia, is named after him.
The first ten US presidents.John Quincy Adams: The son of John Adams, he served 17 years in the House of Representatives after his presidency.
The first ten US presidents.Andrew Jackson: Both pistols misfired in the first assassination attempt on a president, in 1835.
The first ten US presidents.Martin Van Buren: Known as 'Old Kinderhook', his nickname helped popularise the expression 'OK'.
The first ten US presidents.William Henry Harrison: He gave the longest inaugural address and then died after just 31 days, the shortest presidency.
The first ten US presidents.John Tyler: The first vice president to take over after a president died, and he fathered 15 children, the most of any president.

Decode the Roman numerals.Rocky IV: Sylvester Stallone wrote, directed and starred in this 1985 film, where Rocky faces the Soviet boxer Ivan Drago.
Decode the Roman numerals.Henry VIII: The Tudor king was a keen musician, and 'Pastime with Good Company' is a song attributed to him.
Decode the Roman numerals.Star Wars: Episode IX: The Rise of Skywalker, from 2019, concluded the nine-film Skywalker saga that began in 1977.
Decode the Roman numerals.Louis XIV: The 'Sun King' reigned for 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch, and built Versailles.
Decode the Roman numerals.Pope Benedict XVI: In 2013 he became the first pope in about 600 years to resign, rather than serve for life.
Decode the Roman numerals.Pope John XXIII: He picked a name already used by a medieval antipope, and called the Second Vatican Council in 1962.
Decode the Roman numerals.Super Bowl XL: The Steelers won this 2006 game, in Detroit, while the NFL's use of numerals goes back to the fifth game.
Decode the Roman numerals.Super Bowl LX: The league once dropped numerals for 'Super Bowl 50', since a lone 'L' looked odd, then went back to them.
Decode the Roman numerals.The year MCMLXIX: In 1969 Apollo 11 landed on the Moon and the Woodstock festival took place.
Decode the Roman numerals.The year MMXXVI: This is the year of the first 48-team World Cup, hosted by the US, Canada and Mexico, and of the US 250th anniversary.

When these pyramids were built.Step Pyramid of Djoser: Imhotep's design of this six-step stone tomb is often counted as the first large stone building in the world.
When these pyramids were built.Great Pyramid of Giza: It was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for about 3,800 years, until Lincoln Cathedral surpassed it in the 1300s.
When these pyramids were built.Taharqa's pyramid at Nuri: The Kushite pharaoh who ruled Egypt from Nubia appears in the Bible as Tirhakah; his pyramid is in what is now Sudan.
When these pyramids were built.Royal pyramids of Meroë: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt; the ones at Meroë are smaller and have much steeper sides.
When these pyramids were built.Pyramid of Cestius, Rome: This tomb of a Roman magistrate was reportedly built within 330 days, and it now forms part of the city's walls.
When these pyramids were built.Pyramid of the Sun: Teotihuacan was already ancient when the Aztecs named it, and nobody knows what its builders called it.
When these pyramids were built.Tikal Temple I: Temple IV at this Maya city doubled as the rebel base in Star Wars, and Temple I held a ruler's tomb.
When these pyramids were built.El Castillo, Chichén Itzá: Its four stairways have 365 steps in total, and at the equinoxes, the shadow of a snake slides down.
When these pyramids were built.Templo Mayor, Tenochtitlan: Electricity workers rediscovered the Aztec temple in 1978 under Mexico City, which led to the digging up of the site.
When these pyramids were built.Candi Sukuh, Java: Its terraced pyramid shape recalls Maya temples, but no link exists, and the carvings are Javanese Hindu.

Middle-earth events in story order.Bilbo finds the Ring: Bilbo found the Ring in Gollum's cave under the Misty Mountains, winning it, he claimed, in a riddle game.
Middle-earth events in story order.Smaug is slain: Bard the Bowman killed Smaug with a black arrow after a thrush told him about a bare patch on the dragon's chest.
Middle-earth events in story order.Bilbo's farewell party: Bilbo's 111th birthday party ended when he slipped on the Ring and vanished in front of the guests.
Middle-earth events in story order.The Council of Elrond: At Rivendell, Elves, Dwarves, Men and Hobbits agreed the Ring must be destroyed, and chose nine to form the Fellowship.
Middle-earth events in story order.Gandalf falls in Moria: Gandalf fought the Balrog on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm and fell, but returned as Gandalf the White.
Middle-earth events in story order.Boromir dies: Boromir tried to take the Ring, then redeemed himself by defending Merry and Pippin from Uruk-hai until his death.
Middle-earth events in story order.Battle of Helm's Deep: At the Hornburg, Rohan's outnumbered defenders held until Gandalf appeared at dawn with Erkenbrand's riders.
Middle-earth events in story order.The Ring is destroyed: Gollum bit off Frodo's finger and fell into Mount Doom with the Ring; March 25 is now Tolkien Reading Day.
Middle-earth events in story order.Aragorn is crowned: Aragorn was crowned King Elessar in Minas Tirith, and Gandalf himself set the crown on his head before cheering crowds.
Middle-earth events in story order.Frodo sails West: Frodo, wounded in spirit, sailed from the Grey Havens with Bilbo, Gandalf and the Elves to the Undying Lands.

Middle Eastern countries by area.Bahrain: Bahrain is an island nation linked to Saudi Arabia by the 25 km King Fahd Causeway, and was long famous for pearl diving.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Qatar: Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup, the first in the Arab world, and it sits atop one of the world's largest natural gas fields.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Israel: Israel's Dead Sea shore, shared with Jordan, is the lowest land on Earth, around 430 m below sea level.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Jordan: Jordan's Petra, a city carved into rose-colored rock by the Nabataeans, was lost to the West until 1812.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Syria: Damascus, Syria's capital, is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Oman: Oman has traded frankincense, a resin from Boswellia trees in the Dhofar region, for thousands of years.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Iraq: In the Sumerian south of today's Iraq, cuneiform writing was invented over 5,000 years ago, between the Tigris and the Euphrates.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Turkey: Istanbul straddles two continents, split by the Bosphorus strait, and is the largest city in Turkey.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Iran: Iran's Persian civilization stretches back over 2,500 years, to the Achaemenid Empire founded by Cyrus the Great.
Middle Eastern countries by area.Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia holds Mecca and Medina, and the Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter, the largest continuous sand desert on Earth.

Brewing beer, step by step.Malt the barley: Barley is soaked so it sprouts, then kilned; sprouting turns starches into fermentable sugars, and the kiln's heat sets the beer's color.
Brewing beer, step by step.Mill the grain: Brewers crack the malt rather than grind it to flour, so the husks stay intact and later act as a natural filter bed.
Brewing beer, step by step.Mash: Soaking crushed malt in water at about 65 °C lets enzymes turn its starches into sugars, making a sweet liquid.
Brewing beer, step by step.Lauter off the wort: Lauter comes from the German for to clarify; the sweet liquid, called wort, drains through the grain bed, which acts as a filter.
Brewing beer, step by step.Boil with hops: Hops, relatives of cannabis, add bitterness and aroma, and their acids also act as a natural preservative.
Brewing beer, step by step.Cool the wort: Wort must be cooled quickly, since warm, sugary liquid invites bacteria; brewers use a heat exchanger or immersion chiller.
Brewing beer, step by step.Pitch the yeast: To pitch means to add, and brewers pitch millions of yeast cells per milliliter, which eat sugar and make alcohol and carbon dioxide.
Brewing beer, step by step.Ferment: Ales ferment warm with top-fermenting yeast, lagers cold with bottom-fermenting yeast, taking from days to a few weeks.
Brewing beer, step by step.Condition: Lagering takes its name from the German word for to store; cold conditioning for weeks mellows harsh flavors.
Brewing beer, step by step.Package: Cans and brown bottles shield beer from light, which can make it skunky by reacting with hop compounds.

Harry Potter events in story order.Harry learns he's a wizard: Hagrid's 'Yer a wizard, Harry' arrives on Harry's eleventh birthday, after Uncle Vernon fails to keep the letters out.
Harry Potter events in story order.The Basilisk is slain: Harry kills the monster in the Chamber of Secrets with Gryffindor's sword, and a broken fang later destroys Horcruxes.
Harry Potter events in story order.Buckbeak escapes execution: Harry and Hermione use her Time-Turner to rescue the hippogriff, and Harry's Patronus saves them from dementors.
Harry Potter events in story order.Cedric Diggory dies: At the end of the Triwizard Tournament, Peter Pettigrew kills Cedric on Voldemort's order, marking Voldemort's return.
Harry Potter events in story order.Dumbledore's Army forms: Banned by Umbridge from practical spellwork, students meet secretly in the Room of Requirement to learn defence.
Harry Potter events in story order.Sirius Black dies: He falls through the veil in the Department of Mysteries during a duel with Bellatrix Lestrange.
Harry Potter events in story order.Dumbledore dies: Killed on the Astronomy Tower by Snape; book 7 reveals the two had agreed the act beforehand.
Harry Potter events in story order.Bill and Fleur's wedding: News that the Ministry has fallen interrupts the reception, and Harry, Ron and Hermione flee into hiding.
Harry Potter events in story order.Battle of Hogwarts: Voldemort's army attacks the castle, and defenders include teachers, students, and even the house-elves led by Kreacher.
Harry Potter events in story order.Nineteen years later: At King's Cross, Harry sends off his son Albus Severus, named after two headmasters of Hogwarts.

The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.High school diploma: The word diploma comes from Greek for a folded document.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Associate degree: Many US students use it as a cheaper first step toward a four-year degree by transferring credits.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Bachelor's degree: The title comes from medieval Latin 'baccalarius', a young trainee ranking below a master.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Master's degree: In medieval universities, a 'master' was a licensed teacher, which is where the title comes from.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Doctorate: 'Doctor' is Latin for teacher, and Yale awarded the first American PhDs in 1861.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Postdoctoral fellow: Postdocs power much of modern science, usually on short fixed-term contracts of a few years.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Assistant professor: On the US tenure track, this is the entry rank, and tenure review typically comes after about six years.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Associate professor: In the US, promotion to this rank usually comes with tenure, a protection rooted in academic freedom.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Full professor: Britain uses 'professor' for a rare senior chair, whereas the US applies it more widely to many staff.
The academic ladder, from diploma to eme.Professor emeritus: From Latin meaning 'having earned by service', emeriti keep the title after retirement, often with library access.

Caribbean islands by area.Aruba: Sits just off Venezuela's coast, outside the main hurricane belt, which helps explain its famously dry, sunny weather.
Caribbean islands by area.Grenada: Called the Spice Isle, it is among the world's top nutmeg producers, and a nutmeg appears on its national flag.
Caribbean islands by area.Barbados: The easternmost Caribbean island, widely seen as the birthplace of rum, it became independent from Britain in 1966.
Caribbean islands by area.Martinique: An overseas region of France, so it uses the euro. Napoleon's first wife, Josephine, was born here.
Caribbean islands by area.Guadeloupe: Shaped like a butterfly, it is really two main islands, Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre, split by a narrow channel.
Caribbean islands by area.Trinidad: Birthplace of calypso and the steelpan, an instrument invented in the 20th century. It is the larger half of Trinidad and Tobago.
Caribbean islands by area.Puerto Rico: A US territory whose people are US citizens. Its Arecibo dish was once the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.
Caribbean islands by area.Jamaica: Home of reggae and sprinter Usain Bolt, and the source of prized Blue Mountain coffee, grown high in its eastern hills.
Caribbean islands by area.Hispaniola: Columbus landed here in 1492. Today it is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, one of few islands split between two nations.
Caribbean islands by area.Cuba: The largest Caribbean island is home to the bee hummingbird, the smallest bird on Earth, weighing about two grams.

Book series, by number of books.His Dark Materials: Philip Pullman's trilogy opens with Northern Lights, called The Golden Compass in the US, and features animal souls called daemons.
Book series, by number of books.Ferrante's Neapolitan Novels: Elena Ferrante's saga begins with My Brilliant Friend and follows two Neapolitan friends across decades.
Book series, by number of books.Douglas Adams's Hitchhiker: Called a 'trilogy in five parts', it began as a BBC radio comedy in 1978.
Book series, by number of books.Frank Herbert's Dune books: Frank Herbert wrote six Dune novels, and his son Brian continued the saga afterward.
Book series, by number of books.Harry Potter (main): The seven books have sold hundreds of millions of copies in dozens of languages.
Book series, by number of books.A Series of Unfortunate Events: Lemony Snicket is the pen name of Daniel Handler. The books warn readers to look away.
Book series, by number of books.The Wheel of Time (main): Robert Jordan died in 2007 before finishing it, and Brandon Sanderson completed the last three volumes.
Book series, by number of books.Discworld: Terry Pratchett's comic fantasy set on a flat world carried by four elephants on a giant turtle runs to 41 novels.
Book series, by number of books.Goosebumps (original): R. L. Stine's series of kid-friendly horror stories sold hundreds of millions of copies.
Book series, by number of books.Baby-Sitters Club (main): Ann M. Martin started it in 1986, and ghostwriters wrote many later volumes.

Football clubs, by founding.Sheffield FC: Founded in 1857, it's recognized by Guinness as the world's oldest football club, and still plays in the lower leagues.
Football clubs, by founding.Notts County: The oldest professional football club in the world, nicknamed the Magpies, wearing black and white stripes.
Football clubs, by founding.Rangers: Founded by friends who rowed on the Clyde, it borrowed its name from an English rugby club and is among world football's most decorated sides.
Football clubs, by founding.Manchester United: Founded as Newton Heath, a railway workers' side, it only became Manchester United in 1902, to avoid bankruptcy.
Football clubs, by founding.Arsenal: Founded by workers at the Royal Arsenal munitions factory in southeast London, the club later moved north across the city.
Football clubs, by founding.Liverpool: After Everton left Anfield in a rent dispute, John Houlding founded the club to fill the ground. It has won six European Cups.
Football clubs, by founding.Juventus: Founded by schoolboys in Turin, the club's black-and-white stripes were copied from Notts County, whose shirts a player had brought from England.
Football clubs, by founding.Barcelona: Founded by Swiss businessman Joan Gamper, the club's motto 'Més que un club' means 'more than a club'.
Football clubs, by founding.Real Madrid: Named 'Real' (royal) by King Alfonso XIII in 1920, it has won more European Cups than any other club, with 15 so far.
Football clubs, by founding.Paris Saint-Germain: Founded in 1970 as a merger, it's the youngest on this list, and Qatari ownership turned it into a European power.

World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Crystal Palace, London: Joseph Paxton, a gardener by training, designed this iron-and-glass hall; it was later moved to Sydenham and burned down in 1936.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Eiffel Tower, Paris: Built for the 1889 fair, it was meant to be temporary, and was saved partly by its use as a radio antenna.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Original Ferris Wheel, Chicago: Built to rival the Eiffel Tower at the Chicago fair, it stood 80 m tall and carried 36 cars.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Trylon and Perisphere, NY: These twin symbols of the 1939 New York World's Fair were scrapped for metal during World War II.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Atomium, Brussels: The giant iron-crystal model is magnified 165 billion times, and has nine spheres you can walk through.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Space Needle, Seattle: Built for the 1962 fair, it went up in about 400 days, and its revolving restaurant gave Seattle its icon.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Habitat 67, Montreal: Moshe Safdie's stacked concrete homes grew from his architecture thesis, and still house residents today.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Tower of the Sun, Osaka: Taro Okamoto's sculpture, with its three faces, survived the fair's demolition and still stands in Osaka.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.China Pavilion, Shanghai: The vermilion pavilion, nicknamed the 'Crown of the East', hosted a record 73 million visitors to its Expo.
World's Fair landmarks, by Expo year.Grand Ring, Osaka: Sou Fujimoto's ring is a vast timber structure about 2 km around, recognised as the largest wooden building in the world.

Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Sugar found in beets: Andreas Marggraf found that sugar from beets was the same as from cane, and that opened the door to a European sugar industry.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Sugar cube invented: Jakob Christoph Rad of Moravia invented the sugar cube, and his wife had reportedly cut her finger on a sugar loaf.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Saccharin discovered: Saccharin was discovered by accident when a chemist, Constantin Fahlberg, noticed a sweet taste on his hands after lab work.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Cyclamate discovered: Cyclamate was discovered by a graduate student who noticed a sweet taste on a cigarette, and it was later banned in the US.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.High-fructose syrup process: High-fructose corn syrup was developed in Japan and the US, and it spread quickly in soft drinks.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Aspartame discovered: Aspartame was found by chemist James Schlatter, who licked his finger while working on an ulcer drug.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Acesulfame K discovered: Acesulfame K was discovered by accident in Germany, and it's often blended with other sweeteners.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Sucralose discovered: Sucralose was discovered at a London college when a researcher mistook a request to test for a request to taste.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Aspartame approved in the US: The FDA approved aspartame for dry foods in 1981, and it later became a staple in diet drinks.
Milestones in the history of sweeteners.Stevia extract cleared in US: Stevia comes from a South American plant used for centuries by the Guarani, and it's about 200 times sweeter than sugar.

Operating systems by first release.Unix: Unix was developed at Bell Labs, and it influenced Linux, macOS and Android.
Operating systems by first release.CP/M: CP/M was the leading OS for early microcomputers, and MS-DOS borrowed ideas from it.
Operating systems by first release.MS-DOS: MS-DOS came with the IBM PC, and it launched Microsoft's rise, even though Microsoft bought its base from Seattle Computer Products.
Operating systems by first release.Mac System 1: The first Mac's System 1 introduced the desktop with icons and mouse, and it fit on a single floppy disk.
Operating systems by first release.AmigaOS: AmigaOS was ahead of its time with multitasking and color graphics, and it had a loyal fan community.
Operating systems by first release.Linux: Linus Torvalds posted that he was building a free OS just a hobby, and Linux now runs most servers and Android phones.
Operating systems by first release.Mac OS X: Mac OS X was built on Unix, and it came out after Apple bought NeXT, which brought back Steve Jobs.
Operating systems by first release.iPhone OS: The first iPhone ran iPhone OS, which wasn't called iOS until 2010, and it had no app store at first.
Operating systems by first release.Android: Android was started in 2003 by a different company, and Google bought it in 2005, before the first phone arrived.
Operating systems by first release.ChromeOS: ChromeOS is built around the Chrome browser, and it runs on cheap Chromebooks widely used in schools.

When these mega-dams were completed.Hoover Dam: Hoover Dam was built in the Great Depression on the Colorado River, and it created Lake Mead, the largest US reservoir.
When these mega-dams were completed.Grand Coulee Dam: Grand Coulee Dam in Washington is the largest US concrete structure, and it powered wartime plutonium production.
When these mega-dams were completed.Kariba Dam: Kariba Dam on the Zambezi created one of the world's largest reservoirs, and it forced the relocation of tens of thousands of Tonga people.
When these mega-dams were completed.Grande Dixence: Grande Dixence in Switzerland is the tallest gravity dam in the world at 285 m, and it's in the Alps.
When these mega-dams were completed.Glen Canyon Dam: Glen Canyon Dam created Lake Powell, and it's a famous reservoir of the Colorado River.
When these mega-dams were completed.Aswan High Dam: Aswan High Dam tamed the Nile floods, and it created Lake Nasser and required moving ancient temples like Abu Simbel.
When these mega-dams were completed.Tarbela Dam: Tarbela Dam in Pakistan is the largest earth-filled dam in the world, and it sits on the Indus.
When these mega-dams were completed.Itaipu Dam: Itaipu Dam on the Brazil-Paraguay border supplies most of Paraguay's electricity, and it's among the largest hydro plants.
When these mega-dams were completed.Three Gorges Dam: Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze is the world's largest power station, and it displaced over a million people.
When these mega-dams were completed.Baihetan Dam: Baihetan Dam in China is among the biggest hydropower plants, and it's built on the Jinsha River.

When these TV dramas aired their final e.Twin Peaks (original run): Lynch and Frost's mystery asked who killed Laura Palmer, and it ended on a famous cliffhanger. A revival followed 26 years later.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.The X-Files (original run): Mulder and Scully chased the paranormal for nine seasons before this finale. The show returned for new episodes in 2016.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.The West Wing: Aaron Sorkin's White House drama won the Emmy for best drama four years running. Its walk-and-talk scenes became a TV trademark.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.The Sopranos: Its last scene cuts abruptly to black mid-song, as Journey's "Don't Stop Believin'" plays. Fans argued about what it meant for years.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.ER: This hospital drama ran 15 seasons and made George Clooney a star. Only a few US dramas have lasted longer in primetime.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.Lost: A plane crash on a mysterious island launched this puzzle-box series. Its finale split viewers, and the pilot was among the costliest ever filmed.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.Breaking Bad: The finale, "Felina," closed Walter White's story. The universe kept going with the prequel-style spin-off Better Call Saul.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.Mad Men: This advertising drama ends with a calm meditation scene and a famous Coca-Cola ad. Viewers still debate who created that ad.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.Game of Thrones: Based on George R.R. Martin's novels, it set a record for most Emmys won by a drama series. Its last season was its most divisive.
When these TV dramas aired their final e.Succession: Jesse Armstrong's saga of a feuding media dynasty lasted just four seasons. Nicholas Britell's moody theme tune became a hit in itself.

Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.HMS Challenger expedition: This British expedition circled the globe, sounding the seabed and discovering thousands of new species; it founded oceanography.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Beebe's bathysphere dive: William Beebe and Otis Barton were lowered off Bermuda in a steel ball on a cable to roughly 900 m.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Trieste reaches the bottom: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep, nearly 11 km down, the first crewed dive there.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Project Mohole drills seafloor: An attempt to drill through the crust to the mantle off Mexico; it reached basalt, was cancelled, yet proved deep-sea drilling possible.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Alvin's first dive: The US Navy research submersible has made thousands of dives and helped explore the Titanic in 1986.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Kola Superdeep drilling begins: This Soviet borehole reached about 12.2 km, the deepest humans have ever drilled, finding rocks hotter and wetter than expected.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Hydrothermal vents discovered: Alvin found hot springs on the Galápagos Rift, teeming with life powered by chemicals rather than sunlight.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Titanic wreck found: Robert Ballard found it at about 3,800 m down, 73 years after it sank; the discovery was a cover for Navy submarine surveys.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.James Cameron's solo dive: He piloted a one-man sub, Deepsea Challenger, to the Challenger Deep, the first solo dive to the bottom.
Probing the deep: milestones of explorat.Five Deeps Expedition: Victor Vescovo reached the deepest point in each of the five oceans in a single submersible.

Island nations by population.Tuvalu: Nine tiny atolls, none higher than about 5 m above sea level; its .tv internet domain earns the country a notable share of its income.
Island nations by population.Iceland: Its parliament, the Althing, was founded around 930, making it one of the oldest legislative assemblies in the world.
Island nations by population.Malta: Its Neolithic temples, such as Ġgantija, are older than Stonehenge and Egypt's pyramids.
Island nations by population.Jamaica: Blue Mountain coffee, grown in its misty highlands, is among the world's most prized and expensive beans.
Island nations by population.Ireland: It shares its island with Northern Ireland, and tens of millions of people worldwide claim Irish ancestry, many times the home population.
Island nations by population.Cuba: The Caribbean's largest island; its streets still run on classic 1950s American cars kept alive by decades of improvisation.
Island nations by population.Sri Lanka: Once called Ceylon, it is a top tea exporter and elected the world's first female prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike, in 1960.
Island nations by population.United Kingdom: Most of it sits on Great Britain, Europe's largest island, but it also counts thousands of smaller islands, from Skye to Shetland.
Island nations by population.Japan: Four main islands hold nearly everyone, yet Japan has more than 14,000 islands in all.
Island nations by population.Indonesia: With over 17,000 islands, it is the largest archipelagic nation, and Java alone holds more than half of its people.

Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.Teaspoon: The standard US teaspoon is really about 4.9 ml; labels and medicine doses round it to a neat 5 ml.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.Tablespoon: An Australian tablespoon holds 20 ml, a third more than the US 15 ml, so imported recipes can quietly go wrong.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US fluid ounce: It is about 29.6 ml, while the British imperial fluid ounce is a little smaller, at about 28.4 ml.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US shot glass: A US shot is commonly 1.5 fluid ounces, but legal shot sizes vary from place to place, so bars differ.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US cup: Many countries, including Australia, use a 250 ml metric cup, which is a little bigger than the US cup.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US pint: The imperial pint is 568 ml, about 20 percent bigger than the US pint, so a British pint pour is generous.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US quart: Its name is simply a quarter of a gallon, the same idea as the quarter in a US coin.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.US gallon: The US gallon descends from the old English wine gallon of 231 cubic inches, defined in 1707 under Queen Anne.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.Barrel of oil: The 42-gallon oil barrel traces back to the 1860s Pennsylvania oil fields, long after barrels stopped carrying oil.
Volume: from teaspoon to swimming pool.Olympic swimming pool: A pool 50 m long, 25 m wide and at least 2 m deep holds enough water to fill about 15,000 bathtubs.

When these lighthouses were built.Lighthouse of Alexandria: One of the Seven Wonders, the Pharos gave its name to lighthouses in many languages, like 'phare' in French.
When these lighthouses were built.Tower of Hercules, Spain: The oldest Roman lighthouse still in use, at the northwest tip of Spain.
When these lighthouses were built.Lanterna of Genoa (current): At about 77 m, it is among the world's tallest traditional lighthouses, in Columbus's reputed hometown.
When these lighthouses were built.Cordouan Lighthouse: Nicknamed the 'Versailles of the sea', it stands on a rock in the Gironde estuary.
When these lighthouses were built.Smeaton's Eddystone: John Smeaton's tower pioneered hydraulic cement and interlocking stones, and its top now stands on Plymouth Hoe.
When these lighthouses were built.Bell Rock Lighthouse: Robert Stevenson built the oldest surviving sea-washed lighthouse, miles off the Scottish coast.
When these lighthouses were built.Skerryvore Lighthouse: Built by Alan Stevenson, uncle of Robert Louis Stevenson, it stands about 48 m high.
When these lighthouses were built.Cape Hatteras (current): It was moved 880 m inland in 1999 to escape erosion, and it is the tallest brick lighthouse in the US.
When these lighthouses were built.Fastnet (current tower): Called 'Ireland's Teardrop', it was the last piece of Europe emigrants saw on their way to America.
When these lighthouses were built.Jeddah Light: At around 133 m, it is among the tallest lighthouses ever built.

Garden and town birds by weight.Goldcrest: Europe's smallest bird has a golden crown stripe and weighs about as much as a 20p coin. It survives winters by feeding constantly on tiny insects.
Garden and town birds by weight.Robin: British robins are fiercely territorial, even in winter, and males will attack their own reflection. They became Christmas symbols from the red-coated postmen.
Garden and town birds by weight.House sparrow: Once abundant, it has declined sharply in many cities. It has lived alongside humans for thousands of years and spread with farming around the world.
Garden and town birds by weight.Starling: Starlings can mimic other birds and even phone ringtones. In autumn thousands gather in swirling flocks called murmurations at dusk.
Garden and town birds by weight.Magpie: Magpies are among the few animals that pass the mirror test, hinting at self-awareness. The old belief that they steal shiny things is largely a myth.
Garden and town birds by weight.Feral pigeon: Descended from wild rock doves, city pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of kilometres away. They were used to carry messages in wars.
Garden and town birds by weight.Carrion crow: Crows can use tools, recognise human faces and hold a grudge. Some drop nuts onto roads so passing cars crack them open.
Garden and town birds by weight.Herring gull: Gulls have a red spot on the bill that chicks peck to beg for food. In towns they have become expert thieves of chips from beach tourists.
Garden and town birds by weight.Grey heron: This patient fisher stands motionless in shallows, then strikes with its dagger-like bill. In flight it folds its neck into an S shape.
Garden and town birds by weight.Canada goose: Native to North America, flocks fly in V formations to save energy. They were brought to Britain in the 17th century and are now widespread.

Building a campfire, step by step.Clear a patch of ground: Clearing leaves, grass and twigs down to bare soil stops the fire from spreading. A good spot is sheltered from wind and away from overhanging branches.
Building a campfire, step by step.Make a ring of stones: A ring contains the fire and focuses its heat. Avoid wet river stones, though, as trapped water can turn to steam and make them burst.
Building a campfire, step by step.Pile tinder in the middle: Tinder is thin, dry material that catches a spark, such as birch bark, dry grass or cotton wool. It must be bone dry or it will not light.
Building a campfire, step by step.Lean kindling in a teepee: Pencil-thin sticks lean against each other with gaps for air. A teepee shape draws air upwards, like a chimney, to feed the flame.
Building a campfire, step by step.Light the tinder: Fire needs three things, heat, fuel and oxygen, known as the fire triangle. Matches, lighters or a ferro rod can supply the spark.
Building a campfire, step by step.Blow gently on the flame: A little extra air helps a young flame grow. Blow too hard, however, and you can blow it out.
Building a campfire, step by step.Add bigger sticks: Add fuel in stages, from thin sticks to thicker ones, so each size catches from the one before. Piling on too much too early can smother the fire.
Building a campfire, step by step.Add logs: Dry hardwoods such as oak and ash burn longer and hotter than softwoods. Pine and other resinous woods spit and pop more.
Building a campfire, step by step.Douse with water: Never leave a campfire burning unattended. Pour on plenty of water and listen for hissing, as it needs to be completely out.
Building a campfire, step by step.Stir ashes and douse again: Embers can stay hot under ash for hours, even a day. The rule is to keep dousing until the ashes feel cool to the touch.

The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Douglas Adams born: Born in Cambridge, he conceived the idea while lying drunk in a field in Innsbruck with a copy of a hitchhiking guide.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Radio series: It began as a BBC Radio 4 comedy, with Peter Jones as the voice of the Guide.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.First novel: It opens with the demolition of Arthur Dent's house and then Earth for a hyperspace bypass, and sold millions.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.The Restaurant at the End: The sequel features Milliways, a restaurant at the end of time where diners watch the universe end.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.TV series: The BBC adaptation used hand-drawn animation for the Guide's entries.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Life, the Universe, Everything: It began life as a rejected Doctor Who story idea, which Adams had written as The Krikkitmen.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.So Long, and Thanks for Fish: The fourth book is a love story, in which Arthur returns to Earth and meets Fenchurch.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Mostly Harmless: The fifth book ends with Earth's destruction yet again, and Adams reportedly disliked writing it.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Douglas Adams dies: He died of a heart attack at 49 in California, and fans honour him on Towel Day, May 25.
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy tim.Feature film: Released in 2005, it starred Martin Freeman as Arthur Dent.

Candy, by when it first appeared.Candy corn: Invented by Philadelphia candymaker George Renninger, it was originally called chicken feed.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Tootsie Roll: Created by Austrian immigrant Leo Hirshfeld and named after his daughter's nickname, it was packed in wartime rations.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Hershey's Kisses: Hershey makes tens of millions of these a day, and the origin of the name is uncertain.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Milky Way: Created by Frank Mars, it was named after the malted milk shake, not the galaxy.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Reese's Cups: Harry Burnett Reese, a former Hershey dairy farm worker, invented them in his basement.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Snickers: Mars named it after a family horse, and in the UK it was sold as Marathon until 1990 before the name was changed to match the rest of the world.
Candy, by when it first appeared.M&M's: Named for Mars and Murrie, it was created so soldiers could carry chocolate without it melting.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Jolly Rancher: Founded in Golden, Colorado, by Bill Harmsen, who intended it as a hearty name.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Skittles: First sold in Britain, it arrived in the US in 1979.
Candy, by when it first appeared.Nerds: Created by the Willy Wonka Candy Company, a Nestle brand, with two flavours in each box compartment.
